text:
alex: Hey team — PR #48210 is ready for merge but needs runtime + security eyes before I queue canary. Main changes are routing fallback behavior and a new feature flag `prefer_cost_savings`.
maya: Thanks Alex. @sam can you take runtime perf validation? main risk is tail latency with the new fallback routing.
sam: I can do a perf pass tomorrow morning. Quick Q: does this change default behavior for existing clusters?
alex: No — default is unchanged. We added `prefer_cost_savings: false` in defaults and a migration note. PR includes a short migration script.
jordan: OOO until 15:00 today, but I can scan for authz/data-path touches after that. Any token or header handling changed?
alex: No token/header changes — routing only. I added a note in the PR and a label `security: review-needed` and `security: no-privilege-change` in the description.
maya: @sam when you run perf can you compare 256 and 1024 seq lengths and paste p50/p95/p99? If regression >5% we won't proceed.
sam: Will run on staging with the canary fixture. Command I'm running:
```bash
make perf-test TARGET=canary SEQ_LEN=256,1024 ITER=100
```
ETA EOD PST, will paste numbers here.
ci-bot: CI passed — all checks green :white_check_mark:
maya: Perfect. If runtime numbers look good, I will request an eng-platform approval and slot this in the canary window tomorrow 09:00-11:00.
jordan: Assuming no authz surface changes, I can lgtm after my scan. I'll mark myself as reviewer on the PR.
alex: Thanks all — tagging @eng-platform for visibility. I'll wait for @sam perf numbers and @jordan security ack before requesting final approvals and scheduling the canary.
